newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI "no comment" on EU Lonrho probe.
newsitem.headline: JCI "no comment" on EU Lonrho probe.

text.p: South Africa's JCI Ltd on Friday declined to comment on the European Commission's decision to study a deal in which black South African mining house JCI Ltd plans to buy a large stake in Lonrho Plc.
The Commission said earlier on Friday it would study the deal but stressed that at this stage its interest was purely routine.
JCI spokesman Marc Gonsalves said the company had "no comment at this stage".

JCI on Wednesday announced it had an option to buy 26.8 percent of Lonrho from Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd for 2.5 billion rand, just two days after merger talks between JCI and the British conglomerate were abandoned.
The move solves a problem for Anglo, which was forced by the Commission to place all but 9.99 percent of its Lonrho stake into a trust and seek a sale within two years.
The EU's competition watchdog objected to the purchase on the grounds that it gave the South African giant too much control over the world's platinum market.

A spokesman for European competition commissioner Karel van Miert said on Friday it was far too early to judge whether the move satisfied its decision in April to force Anglo to dispose of its Lonrho holdings.
"We have been informed and are presently studying the details...But we are in no position to make a formal analysis," he said. He could not say how long the process would last.
